entries.clue: Way of printing behind the scenes (6)

blocks.note: a lithographic method: ink passes from plate to rubber roller, then to paper
away from the film or stage set, out of the audience's view

annotation.surface: A printer explaining that the real work of a print shop happens out of sight.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense only appears once you split the answer: OFF SET, which is where things happen behind the scenes.
annotation.definitionFit: Offset lithography is the standard commercial way of printing.

entries.clue: Gold-digger preparing fourteenth run (7-6)

indicatorNotes.preparing: preparing a dish means working its ingredients into a new form, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone after money lining up for yet another attempt, their fourteenth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb or a sporting term, but it is just three letters of fodder joined to FOURTEENTH.
annotation.definitionFit: A gold-digger chases a rich partner, which is exactly what a fortune-hunter does.

entries.clue: Those posing as baby-minders? (7)

blocks.note: people who sit for a portrait or photograph
short for babysitters

annotation.surface: People pretending to be childminders, perhaps to get into a house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Posing as' reads as pretending; here 'posing' means modelling for an artist, and 'as' only joins the two meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: An artist's models are called sitters because they sit for the portrait.

entries.clue: Spear disturbed dirt on net somehow (7)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: disturbed things are knocked out of place, so the letters of DIRT are moved
indicatorNotes.somehow: somehow says the letters come together in some other way, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, added to DIRT
anagram indicator
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A fisherman's spear churning up the mud next to a net.
annotation.walkthrough: The fishing picture is apt: a trident and a net are the weapons of the Roman retiarius gladiator.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: Neptune's three-pronged weapon is one particular sort of spear.

entries.clue: Online viewer has natural trap to get coat back (6)

indicatorNotes.back: back sends the word in the other direction, right to left

blocks.note: a spider's web is a trap nature makes
mac = mackintosh, a British word for a raincoat
reversal indicator: MAC becomes CAM

annotation.surface: Someone watching online who wants their coat returned from a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: A mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat in Britain; turned round it gives CAM.
annotation.definitionFit: A webcam is a camera through which someone views you online.

entries.clue: A long time after start of work, salary given (5)

indicatorNotes.after: after puts the long time second, following the W
indicatorNotes.start of: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of work
'it took ages' = a long time

annotation.surface: Pay arriving only a long while after you start a job.
annotation.walkthrough: Read in order, the clue puts the long time first; 'after' flips it so AGES comes behind W.
annotation.definitionFit: Wages are the pay given for work, much like a salary.

entries.clue: Pal's sprout to dry right out (5)

indicatorNotes.out: out removes something: the R goes out of DRY

blocks.note: a bud is a new sprout on a plant
DRY with R (right) taken out

annotation.surface: A friend's seedling left out to dry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pal's' is 'Pal is', so the apostrophe-s is only a link; R = right is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are informal words for a close friend, BUDDY the more American.

entries.clue: Seat from dilapidated Lancaster dwelling (9,4)

indicatorNotes.dilapidated: a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram of LANCASTER
a dwelling is a home

annotation.surface: A chair salvaged from a ruined house in Lancaster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like a chair, but it is a country seat, the family estate of a noble line; Lancaster is also a royal house, which fits.
annotation.definitionFit: A country seat is a family's long-held estate, its ancestral home.

entries.clue: Composing a piece about hospital while in pain (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so WRITING goes around the H

blocks.note: composing a piece of text is writing it
H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: An author struggling to write while unwell.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an author working through illness; 'in pain' is the definition at the end, and 'while' only joins it on.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone writhing twists about because they are in pain.
annotation.definitionNote: 'in pain' is an adjective phrase; WRITHING is used adjectivally, as in 'lying there writhing'.

entries.clue: Cut off part of the harbour (4)

blocks.note: a verb, used of shortening a dog's tail or deducting from pay
where ships berth

annotation.surface: A section of the harbour sealed off from the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' looks like it describes the harbour, isolated; it is a verb, as in docking pay.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated words share the spelling: a verb for cutting short, and a noun for an enclosed berth where ships load.

entries.clue: French priest always sought at Lourdes (4)

blocks.note: curé is French for a parish priest
Lourdes is a French pilgrimage town where the sick seek miraculous healing

annotation.surface: A French priest who is forever in demand at the shrine of Lourdes.
annotation.walkthrough: Lourdes, in south-west France, draws millions of sick pilgrims hoping for a cure, so the second half is a cryptic definition; the accent on curé is dropped in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Curé is the French word for a parish priest.

entries.clue: Writer, for example, infiltrating suspect sites (8)

indicatorNotes.infiltrating: to infiltrate is to get inside, so SAY goes into the other letters
indicatorNotes.suspect: suspect means dubious, not quite right, so SITES is rearranged

blocks.note: anagram of SITES
'say' = for example, as in 'a fruit, say'

annotation.surface: A writer, perhaps a journalist, sneaking into dodgy locations.
annotation.walkthrough: SITES is rearranged to ES…IST and SAY slips in: ES(SAY)IST.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: someone who writes short prose pieces is one kind of writer.

entries.clue: Make fun of the first crockery collection (3,3)

indicatorNotes.first: the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to tease is to make fun of
first letter of 'the'

annotation.surface: Mocking the earliest set of china someone owned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The first' looks like 'the original one'; it means the first letter of 'the'. The word break moves: TEASE+T becomes TEA SET.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea set is a matching collection of cups, saucers and pot.

entries.clue: Chaperone, English type, entertaining Conservative (6)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain guests is to take them in, so SORT holds the C

blocks.note: E = English
a sort is a type or kind
C = Conservative, the British political party

annotation.surface: A proper English chaperone who happens to be amusing a Tory.
annotation.walkthrough: E then SORT with C inside: E + S(C)ORT. The Conservatives are Britain's main right-wing party, abbreviated C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a person who goes along with someone to protect or supervise them.

entries.clue: Went in and made a record (7)

blocks.note: came into a room or building
wrote an item into a log or ledger

annotation.surface: A singer who walked into the studio and cut a disc.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made a record' suggests music; it means writing an entry, as in a log or ledger.
annotation.definitionFit: To enter is both to go in and to record something in a book.

entries.clue: Cowherd cooking soup (7)

indicatorNotes.cooking: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A farmhand making a pot of soup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cowherd' is placed first so it reads as the cook; the whole word is the fodder, and the answer uses exactly its seven letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, often of clams or fish.

entries.clue: Circle part of courtyard before declamation (8)

indicatorNotes.before: before puts QUAD first, ahead of RANT

blocks.note: a quad (quadrangle) is a college courtyard
a rant is a loud, overblown speech

annotation.surface: Someone holding forth in a courtyard ahead of a formal speech.
annotation.walkthrough: A quad is the square courtyard of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
annotation.definitionFit: Geometry: one quarter of a circle, cut off by two perpendicular radii, is a specific part of it.

entries.clue: Western city to avoid (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the city is Dodge City, Kansas; the clue shortens it to DODGE

blocks.note: a Wild West cattle town in Kansas, usually given with 'City'
sidestep, evade

annotation.surface: A cowboy town best kept away from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Western' is a genre: Dodge City was the classic Wild West town of cowboy films.
annotation.definitionFit: Dodge City is a famous frontier town in Kansas, the setting of many Westerns.

entries.clue: Superior, British in flying boat (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in puts the B inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.flying: things flying are tossed about, so BOAT is rearranged

blocks.note: anagram of BOAT
B = British

annotation.surface: A top-ranking Briton aboard a seaplane.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying boat' is a seaplane, but here the phrase splits into indicator and fodder. 'Superior' is a noun, as in Mother Superior, the head of a religious house.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbot is the superior, the head, of an abbey of monks.

entries.clue: Swimming in fat, even socially? (4)

blocks.note: the literal reading: food dripping with grease
the figurative reading: a person who is smarmy and ingratiating in company

annotation.surface: A plate of fried food that is also too smooth at parties.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is the literal sense, food dripping with fat; 'even socially' adds the figurative one, an oily person being unctuous and ingratiating.
annotation.definitionFit: Oily describes both greasy food and a smarmy, over-smooth person.

entries.clue: Dust kicked about in breeding farm (4)

indicatorNotes.kicked about: something kicked about is knocked all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Dirt thrown up by horses on a stud farm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kicked about' suits the horses in the picture, which is why it reads as scenery rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where horses are kept for breeding.

entries.clue: Building entrance is easy target (4,4)

blocks.note: the door of a barn, a farm building
proverbially too big to miss; a poor shot 'couldn't hit' one

annotation.surface: A burglar noting that the front door is the simplest way in.
annotation.walkthrough: The saying 'he couldn't hit a barn door' mocks a bad shot, so a barn door is proverbially an easy target.
annotation.definitionFit: A barn door is literally the entrance to a barn and figuratively a target impossible to miss.

entries.clue: Minister converts sprite (6)

indicatorNotes.converts: to convert is to change form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A clergyman bringing a fairy to the faith.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Converts' fits the churchman in the surface, bringing souls to the faith, but it only rearranges SPRITE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the religious sense of minister, a member of the clergy, not a government one.

entries.clue: Cloud over hideout with old boat inside (6)

indicatorNotes.inside: the old boat sits inside the hideout

blocks.note: a den is a hideout, as for thieves
Noah's Ark, the boat of the Old Testament

annotation.surface: Skies turning grey over a hidden lair that has an ancient vessel in it.
annotation.walkthrough: D(ARK)EN. 'Cloud over' reads as a noun phrase about weather above the den, but it is the verb, to darken.
annotation.definitionFit: When the sky clouds over, it darkens.
